fields.description:
Routine bodies and the triggers that bind them are edited as copies inside append-only SQLx migrations. Each change restates the whole routine, reviewers see no diff, and two branches that restate one object race so the later migration silently wins. The consumer survey: 263 migrations, 941 routine definitions for 576 routines, 25,112 superseded lines, one routine with 19 versions.

Add to batter-sqlx: a pure, bounded ManagedObjectManifest (routine and trigger entries carrying full CREATE OR REPLACE statements with checksums, explicit retirements, a non-omittable PUBLIC EXECUTE policy, a consumer-named ledger distinct from the SQLx ledger, and a deterministic set digest); a lease entry point that runs the consumer-selected SQLx migrator and then applies the manifest in one transaction on the same connection (retire, create-or-replace, PUBLIC EXECUTE policy, ledger rows with source checksum and rendered catalog hash); and a read-only VerificationPlan axis that compares the ledger with the manifest and recomputes rendered catalog hashes to detect out-of-band DDL. Batter applies and verifies the declared set; content, ownership transfer, grants and migration selection stay downstream.
fields.acceptance_criteria: ADR-013 records the boundary and the ADR-010 invalid-state review for every new public item. Pure manifest validation tests cover every rejection path. Live PostgreSQL 18 tests cover first apply after migrations, idempotent re-apply with identical catalog, retirement of a signature with a dependent trigger, PUBLIC EXECUTE policy, out-of-band drift detected by verification, and a missing-ledger finding; apply without migrate is a compile-fail doctest. The postgres-lifecycle example applies one managed routine and trigger at setup and verifies them at readiness. CHANGELOG, crate README/AGENTS, integrations and architecture docs updated; public-API surface check recorded; scripts/verify.sh green; PR merged with green CI.

Design decisions (before implementation):
1. Public module batter_sqlx::managed: ManagedObjectManifest::new(ledger, PublicExecute, objects, retirements); ManagedObject::{function,procedure,trigger} validate source at construction (lexer mirrors PostgreSQL quoting/comments/dollar quotes and psql's BEGIN ATOMIC heuristic; header must be CREATE OR REPLACE <kind> naming the declared identity, schema-qualified; exactly one statement). Routine identity reuses verification::RoutineSignature; trigger identity is table QualifiedName + Identifier. Retirement::{function,procedure,trigger}. PublicExecute::{Revoke,Unmanaged} has no default. Deterministic SHA-256 set digest over policy, entries and retirements (not the ledger name).
2. Ordering: one consuming entry point PgLease::migrate_and_apply(migrator, &manifest); no apply-only method exists (compile-fail doctest). A session advisory lock keyed by the ledger spans migrate+apply so concurrent replicas cannot interleave one's apply after another's migrations.
3. Apply transaction: create ledger if absent, ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, exact shape check (refuses the SQLx ledger or any other relation). Retire existing triggers, then existing routines, then create-or-replace routines then triggers, then PUBLIC EXECUTE revoke, then ledger rows + set row, COMMIT. Deviation from the brief: an entry whose ledger checksum matches and whose live rendered definition still equals the recorded hash is not re-executed, and retirements run only for objects that still exist. Reason: CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER takes SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE and DROP TRIGGER ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the table even when nothing changes, so re-executing every entry would block writes (and queue convoys) on every startup. Drift is still repaired because a drifted object no longer matches its recorded hash.
4. Each executed body must touch exactly its declared identity (xmin = current xid) and kind; otherwise the transaction is abandoned with IdentityMismatch. Rendering (pg_get_functiondef/pg_get_triggerdef) runs under fixed search_path/DateStyle/IntervalStyle/TimeZone/extra_float_digits/quote_all_identifiers in both apply and verify.
5. Verification axis VerificationPlan::{managed_objects,with_managed_objects}: ACCESS SHARE on the ledger before the snapshot (so a library apply cannot interleave with syscache-based rendering), exact ledger shape, rows vs manifest, set digest, live rendered hash drift, retired objects still present, and PUBLIC EXECUTE under Revoke. New FindingKind/SupportedSurface/UnsupportedSurface/PlanError variants: this breaks exhaustive matches on those exhaustive enums; shipped with a Breaking: changelog note per the repo's exhaustive-enum precedent (ReadinessUnreadyReason), which reconciles the brief's 'new kinds' with its 'additive' instruction.
6. Example: examples/postgres-lifecycle gains one migration, one managed routine and one managed trigger; startup migrates and applies, readiness verifies the SQLx ledger plus managed objects.

Correction to design note 3, from a PostgreSQL 18.6 probe: DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS on an absent trigger holds no table lock (only a NOTICE); dropping an existing trigger takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE; CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER on an unchanged trigger takes SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE until commit; CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION takes no table lock. The skip-unchanged deviation stands on the CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER lock; conditional retirement keeps completed retirements silent and the retired count exact.
